name: Padma River
origin: Continuation of the Ganges, entering Bangladesh at Chapainawabganj
description: The Padma is the main distributary of the Ganges and one of the three mightiest rivers of Bangladesh. It merges with the Jamuna near Goalundo before joining the Meghna, and is famous for hilsa fishing and the Padma Bridge.

name: Jamuna River
origin: Main channel of the Brahmaputra after entering Bangladesh from Assam, India
description: The Jamuna is the Bangladeshi name for the lower course of the Brahmaputra. It is one of the widest braided rivers in the world and is crossed by the Bangabandhu Jamuna Multi-Purpose Bridge.

name: Meghna River
origin: Formed by the union of the Surma and Kushiyara rivers in Sylhet region
description: The Meghna is one of the largest rivers by discharge volume in Bangladesh, carrying the combined waters of the Ganges-Padma and Brahmaputra-Jamuna systems into the Bay of Bengal.

name: Brahmaputra (Old Brahmaputra)
description: The Old Brahmaputra was the main channel before the river shifted course to form the Jamuna in the late 18th century. It still flows through Mymensingh and Jamalpur, supporting agriculture and river life.

name: Surma River
origin: Barak River in India, splitting into Surma and Kushiyara at the border
description: The Surma flows through the scenic haor basin of greater Sylhet and is central to the region's fishing communities and boat culture, feeding wetlands like Tanguar Haor.

name: Karnaphuli River
description: The lifeline of the Chattogram Hill Tracts, the Karnaphuli feeds the Kaptai Lake and Kaptai Hydroelectric Dam, and its estuary forms the natural harbour of Chattogram Port.

name: Teesta River
description: A major transboundary river of the north, the Teesta is central to a long-running water-sharing discussion between Bangladesh and India and supports irrigation across greater Rangpur.

name: Buriganga River
description: Once the main channel of the Ganges, the Buriganga flows past Old Dhaka and Sadarghat and has historically been the lifeline of the capital's river trade, though it now faces heavy pollution.

name: Dhaleshwari River
origin: Distributary of the Jamuna near Tangail
description: A key distributary that separates from the Jamuna and eventually links with the Meghna, historically important for trade routes around Savar and Munshiganj.

name: Rupsha River
origin: Confluence of the Bhairab and Atrai rivers
description: Flowing past Khulna city, the Rupsha connects to the Pashur River toward the Sundarbans and Mongla Port, and is well known for its river ferry (the Rupsha Ferry Ghat).

name: Pashur River
origin: Continuation of the Rupsha River flowing toward the Bay of Bengal
description: The Pashur cuts through the heart of the Sundarbans mangrove forest and serves as the shipping channel for Mongla Port, one of Bangladesh's principal seaports.

name: Halda River
description: One of the only rivers in the world that hosts natural breeding grounds for carp fish, the Halda is ecologically vital to Chattogram's fisheries and hatchery industry.

name: Naf River
description: Forming the natural border between Bangladesh and Myanmar, the Naf River empties into the Bay of Bengal near Teknaf, close to Saint Martin's Island.

name: Atrai River
origin: West Bengal, India, entering through Panchagarh
description: A long, winding river of the northwest that feeds the Chalan Beel wetland system and supports agriculture across greater Rajshahi and Rangpur.

name: Gorai-Madhumati River
origin: Distributary of the Padma near Kushtia
description: Known as the Gorai in its upper reach and the Madhumati downstream, this river is a critical freshwater source for southwestern Bangladesh and the Sundarbans ecosystem.

name: Sitalakhya River
origin: Distributary of the old Brahmaputra near Kapasia
description: A major industrial river that flows through the port town of Narayanganj, historically central to the region's textile and trading economy.
